entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko And 4 Others

Counsel for Applicant :- Iqbal Ahmad,Syed Hasan Ejaz Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Pankaj Bhatia,J.
1. Heard learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. and perused the record.
2. The FIR in question was lodged as a missing person report alleging that the daughter of the informant aged about 17 years was missing and enticed by the applicant.
Subsequently in the statement of the victim recorded under Sections 161 & 164 Cr.P.C., the victim stated that she was taken on a motor cycle to Lucknow and marriage was also solemnized in a temple.
She also stated that physical relations were formed against her consent.
She also stated that the marriage was solemnized against her consent.

sentences.text: 3. The counsel for the applicant also stated that the marriage was solemnized in a temple and undertakes to get the marriage registered after being enlarged on bail, subject to the consent of the victim.

4. Learned A.G.A. opposed the bail prayer.
5.

Considering the two statements where the victim has admitted to going with the applicant to Lucknow on a motor cycle without there being any material to suggest that during the entire journey she has raised any hue and cry, the applicant who is in custody since 18.05.2024 and has no criminal history is enlarged on bail.
Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

6. Let the applicant Karan be released on bail in FIR/ Case Crime No. 119 of 2024, under Sections 342, 376, 363, 366 IPC and section 3/4 POCSO Act, Police Station Laliya, District Balrampur, on his furnishing personal bonds and two reliable sureties of Rs.20,000/- each to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:
(a) The applicant shall an affidavit before the trial Court agreeing to get the marriage registered within a period of three months on being enlarged on bail subject to the consent of the victim.
In case, the applicant resiles from the said undertaking, the victim would be at liberty to move an bail cancellation application.

(b) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(c) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (d) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.

Order Date :- 13.8.2024 Arun  Karan vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko ... on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/138922519/
